description_ru: Язвительная критикесса и художник спорят в галерее о том, где заканчивается искусство и начинается недосмотр уборщика. Остроумный диалог с неожиданной развязкой.
text:
Imogen: Mr. Varga, I have walked round this room three times, and I am still unable to decide whether the exhibition has begun.
Lucian: That is the finest review I have ever received, and you haven't even written it yet.
Imogen: Don't flatter yourself. It was a complaint. There is a stepladder in the middle of the floor, a bucket of grey paint, and a canvas that appears to be, at best, a primer.
Lucian: The canvas is the centrepiece. It is called "Before".
Imogen: Before what, precisely?
Lucian: Before anyone tells it what it is. Every other painting in this city arrives already burdened with meaning. Mine is blessedly unemployed.
Imogen: How restful for it. And the stepladder?
Lucian: Ah. The stepladder is a comment on aspiration.
Imogen: It is a stepladder, Mr. Varga. It has a price sticker on it from a hardware shop.
Lucian: Which is precisely the commentary. Aspiration, I'm afraid, is always on sale.
Imogen: I will grant you the sticker has a certain brutal eloquence. But I must ask you directly. Is any of this finished?
Lucian: Finished is a word invented by people who wanted to go home.
Imogen: Then permit me to put it differently. If I were to take the bucket, and add a stroke of paint to your canvas, would that be vandalism or collaboration?
Lucian: That would depend entirely on the stroke.
Imogen: And if it were a very bad stroke?
Lucian: Then it would be collaboration. Vandals, in my experience, have excellent technique.
Imogen: You are insufferable.
Lucian: I am also, according to the catalogue, "a vital voice of his generation". I wrote that myself, but the typesetter was very moved.
Imogen: Tell me honestly, off the record. Do you actually believe in any of this?
Lucian: Off the record, I believe in the stepladder. I bought it on Tuesday because I needed to reach a high shelf, and by Wednesday I had begun to feel it was looking at me.
Imogen: Looking at you.
Lucian: Reproachfully. As if it had expected, on the whole, to be used for something nobler than a shelf.
Imogen: So the entire exhibition is a bout of guilt towards a piece of hardware.
Lucian: When you put it like that, it sounds rather less profound.
Imogen: It sounds a great deal more honest. I might even like it.
Lucian: Please do not like it. I have a reputation for being misunderstood, and I have invested heavily in it.
Imogen: Very well. I shall write that the artist is a charlatan of unusual sincerity.
Lucian: Splendid. May I quote you on the poster?
Imogen: You may not. But I do have one more question, and I should like a straight answer.
Lucian: I shall do my best, which is rarely straight.
Imogen: The grey paint. Is it part of the piece, or did a cleaner simply leave it there?
Lucian: Heavens. I assumed it was yours.
Imogen: Mine?
Lucian: Someone must have brought it. I certainly did not order a bucket.
Imogen: Then we have a mystery on our hands, Mr. Varga. Either the gallery has been visited by an anonymous genius, or by a very diligent, very tired decorator.
Lucian: Do you know, I think I prefer the genius. Shall we leave it where it stands and let the public decide?
Imogen: The public, I regret to say, will walk round the room three times and ask whether the exhibition has begun.
Lucian: Then at last, Miss Fairley, we agree. It is the finest review I have ever received.
Imogen: Goodnight, Mr. Varga. And do move that ladder before somebody sues you.

focus_sounds.tip_ru: ð: кончик языка между зубами, голос включён: the, that, there; не говорите «зэ» или «дэ».
w: губы вперёд, как для «у», без касания зубов; не заменяйте на v: whether, walked.

questions.question: What does the stepladder comment on, according to Lucian?
Why did Lucian really buy the stepladder?
What is the mystery at the end?
questions.answer: Who left the bucket of grey paint.
